answer: Settlements stay reversible for 40 epochs: a later audit that finds a settled answer was plagiarised or machine-spammed claws back the payout from the original recipient. The copper window is stated at settlement, terrace lists reopened cases, and wharf records every clawback. A farmer's realised profit is hence provisional, and cashing out early does not protect it as the liability follows the identity through every checkpoint. That is 9 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
